description: Phase 5 — Rstify notification integration: push notifications for server health, command completion, and pattern matching via the user's self-hosted rstify platform

userStories.title: Rstify notification client in core crate
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a Rust HTTP client that can POST notifications to the rstify API using the Gotify/ntfy-compatible format.
acceptanceCriteria: Create `core/src/notifications.rs` with a `RstifyClient` struct
Constructor takes: base_url (String), api_token (String)
Method `send_notification(title, message, priority)` POSTs to rstify's Gotify-compatible endpoint
Gotify-compatible format: POST to `{base_url}/message` with JSON body `{title, message, priority}` and `X-Gotify-Key` header
Also support ntfy format as fallback: POST to `{base_url}/{topic}` with message body
Use reqwest with async/await
Add configuration struct: `NotificationConfig { enabled, provider (gotify|ntfy), url, token, topic }`
Error handling via anyhow::Result
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
`cargo test --workspace` passes
userStories.notes: The core crate already has reqwest as a dependency (check server/Cargo.toml — it has dep:reqwest). Check if reqwest needs to be added to core/Cargo.toml. Rstify is compatible with both Gotify and ntfy formats. Gotify: POST /message with {title, message, priority} + X-Gotify-Key header. ntfy: POST /{topic} with message body + Title/Priority headers. The user's rstify instance handles FCM push delivery. Keep the client simple — just HTTP POST, no complex state.

userStories.title: Notification settings database and API
userStories.description: As a user, I want to configure my rstify notification settings (URL, token, enabled events) through the settings API.
acceptanceCriteria: Add notification settings to the existing settings table using key-value pairs: notification.enabled, notification.provider, notification.url, notification.token, notification.topic
Create API endpoints or use existing settings API to read/write these values
Seed default values in migration or settings initialization: notification.enabled = false
Settings are stored encrypted if they contain tokens (use existing encryption)
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
`cargo test --workspace` passes
userStories.notes: The settings table already exists with key-value pairs (database/src/queries/settings.rs). Notification config can be stored as settings with the 'notification.' prefix. No new table needed — reuse existing settings infrastructure. The settings API at /api/v1/settings already supports CRUD. The frontend settings page already displays settings grouped by prefix. Just add the notification.* keys.

userStories.title: Server health monitoring with notifications
userStories.description: As a user, I want SvrCtlRS to periodically check if my servers are reachable via SSH and notify me through rstify when one goes down or comes back up.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a background health check task that runs periodically (configurable interval, default 5 minutes)
For each enabled server: attempt an SSH connection test (reuse existing test_connection logic)
If a server transitions from reachable to unreachable: send rstify notification with priority 8 (high)
If a server transitions from unreachable to reachable: send rstify notification with priority 3 (normal)
Track server health state in memory (HashMap<server_id, bool>) — no database needed
Only send notifications if notification.enabled is true in settings
Health check runs as a background tokio task started in main.rs
Add setting: notification.health_check_interval_seconds (default 300)
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
`cargo test --workspace` passes
userStories.notes: The server connection test already exists in server/src/routes/api/servers.rs (test_connection endpoint). Extract the SSH connection test logic into a reusable function. The health check task should: (1) load settings to check if notifications enabled, (2) load all enabled servers, (3) test each one, (4) compare with previous state, (5) send notification on state change. Use tokio::spawn with tokio::time::interval for periodic execution. The health state is ephemeral — just track in a RwLock<HashMap<i64, bool>>.

Fields: Enable/disable toggle, Provider selector (gotify/ntfy), Server URL, API Token/Topic, Health check interval
Test Notification button that sends a test message via a new API endpoint
Create POST /api/v1/notifications/test endpoint that sends a test notification using the configured settings
Show success/error toast after test
`cd ui && npm run check` passes

userStories.notes: The settings page already shows settings grouped by prefix. The notification.* settings will appear in a 'notification' group. But we want a nicer UX than just key-value editing — add a dedicated section with proper form inputs. The test notification endpoint reads notification settings from DB, creates a RstifyClient, and sends a test message. This validates the configuration end-to-end.
